## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

SensorFreshnessWindow — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/Freshness.kt

## Trigger

MainRacePageViewModel reading heart-rate and speed samples each tick, via SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate and PaceCalculator.smoothedPace — observed

## Today

`SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate` (Freshness.kt) computes `age = now - lastReadingAt`
and returns `Fresh` whenever `age <= WINDOW_MS`. A `lastReadingAt` after `now` —
a sample timestamped in the future — makes `age` negative, and a negative age is
`<= WINDOW_MS`, so the value is returned as `Fresh`.

`PaceCalculator.smoothedPace` (PaceCalculator.kt) has the identical defect,
independently: it filters `speedSamples` with
`now - sample.atElapsedRealtime <= SMOOTHING_WINDOW_MS`, the same one-sided
comparison, so a sample with `atElapsedRealtime` after `now` is kept in the
average instead of being excluded. This filter does not call
`SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate` and is not fixed by changing it.

Both callers are reached from MainRacePageViewModel.kt: `evaluate` at line 239
(heart rate) and `smoothedPace` at line 168 (speed), on every recomposition
tick using the current monotonic `now`.

## Expected

`SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate` rejects a negative age — `lastReadingAt` after
`now` — as `Stale`, in addition to an age past `WINDOW_MS`. A reading that
cannot exist yet must never be treated as fresh.

Second gap, same defect, independent bearer: `PaceCalculator.smoothedPace`'s
own window filter (line 49 of PaceCalculator.kt) must apply the same guard —
excluding any sample whose `atElapsedRealtime` is after `now` — since it does
not delegate to `SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate` and fixing the latter alone
leaves this one unchanged.
